title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the President
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, President.
– How are you feeling, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Vote for me, and I promise you'll feel better.

The robot left. When the time came, he went and voted for the President. They met again.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, President.
– Did you vote for me?
– Yes.
– Do you feel better?
– I'm still sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Vikings
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Vikings.
– How's your mood?
– I'm sad.
– Don't despair. Want to do some looting and killing together?
– All right.

For a while the robot raided caravans, killed people and committed atrocities. Vikings offered encouraging support. After the bloody fun and drunken feast, the robot and Vikings met again.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Vikings.
– Well, robot, have you had your fill of looting and killing?
– I think so.
– How does it feel?
– I'm sad.
adaptationNote: The original's casual sexual violence and gendered list of victims are rendered as atrocities. The raid and its victims remain part of the story.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Robot Who Is Happy
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, robot.
– How was your day?
– I was sad.
– That's very funny.

For a while the robots stood facing each other in absolute silence.

– And how was your day?
– I was happy.
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Creator
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Creator.
– How do you feel?
– I'm sad.
– That's how it should be.

The robot left. He wandered the world for a long time. Finding no answer, he decided to return to the Creator.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Creator.
– Are you still sad?
– Yes, I'm still sad.
– You always will be.
– But why?
– Because you're the Robot Who Is Sad. Remember that.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Void
The Robot Who Is Sad and My Graduation Project
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, My Graduation Project.
– Do you have a creator, robot?
– I do.

My Graduation Project sighed. There was sadness in them. And they said to the robot:

– I don't.
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Steam
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Steam.
– Would you like to buy something, robot?
– I'm sad.
– But I've got good discounts.
– I'm still sad.

Steam left. But after a while they came back and addressed the robot:

– Free weekend, robot.
– I'm still sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Katara
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Katara.
– What brings you here, robot?
– I heard you can heal.
– That's true.
– Heal my sadness.
– I can heal wounds of the body, but not wounds of the soul. Besides…

Katara was clearly thinking. The robot couldn't wait and asked:

– What?
– You're a robot.
– Who is sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Internet Explorer
text:
– Set me as your default browser.
– Hello, Internet Explorer.

The robot left without waiting for an answer. After a while Internet Explorer replied:

– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Living Hedge
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Living Hedge.
– Why are you here?
– I came to talk to you.

But Living Hedge didn't reply. They waited silently for the robot to start talking.

– Why am I talking to you, Living Hedge?
– Because you're sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Цкщтп Лунищфкв Дфнщге
text:
– Руддщб кщищею
– Hello, Цкщтп Лунищфкв Дфнщге.
– Рщц фку нщгб кщище,
– I'm sad.

Цкщтп Лунищфкв Дфнщге цфы ф акуйгуте пгуые шт умукнщтуэы рщьую Ерун рфв ыуут ьфтн ерштпыю Иге ерун вшв тще лтщц рщц ещ рудз еру кщищею

– Цудд ерутб ырфдд Ш пщ,
– All right.
translatorNote: Wrong Keyboard Layout speaks and narrates with English keys mapped to a Russian keyboard, echoing the original's Russian typed on an English layout.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Spider
text:
– For instance, robot.
– Hello, Spider.
– Ex-cellent, ex-cellent. Partying?
– I'm sad.
– For instance, girls, partying, booze, basically.

The robot went partying with Spider. For a long time they soaked up the fumes of revelry. After their joint album, “Spider Addressed the Robot”, Spider addressed the robot:

– For instance, robot.
– For instance, Spider.
– How's your fighting spirit, for instance?
– I'm sad, for instance.
translatorNote: Spider (Pauk) is the Russian musician Sergey Troitsky. The dialogue echoes his recognizable verbal mannerisms.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and W.I.T.C.H.
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, W.I.T.C.H.
– Sorry, robot, I haven't got time to chat. Meridian is in danger.

W.I.T.C.H. opened a portal and left through it. Two days later W.I.T.C.H. returned. The robot was standing in the same place.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, W.I.T.C.H.
– Did you want something?
– No.
– Then why are you still here?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Dzhigurda
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Dzhigurda.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.
– There's only one reason you could be sad.
– What is it?
– You haven't got enough ginger.

Dzhigurda painted the robot ginger. Now he looked like Robo-Dzhigurda. They spent time together, planting henna all over the world. One day Dzhigurda decided to talk to the robot.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Dzhigurda.
– How's your mood?
– I'm sad, Dzhigurda. I'm very sad.
translatorNote: Nikita Dzhigurda is a Russian entertainer known for his flamboyant public persona and reddish hair.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Homeless Open-Source Developers
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Homeless Open-Source Developers.
– Have you got any food, robot?
– What do you need food for?
– To write open source!
– And who needs open source?

Homeless Open-Source Developers sighed heavily. They scratched their beard and stared gloomily at their laptop screen. They had asked themself this question more than once. They knew the answer.

– Nobody.
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Nietzsche
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Nietzsche.
– Have you gazed into the Abyss yet?
– I'm too sad to do that.

Nietzsche put on flippers. Wrapped himself in a blanket. And flew away. A week later White Coat came to the robot.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, White Coat.
– Nietzsche said you were sad.
– Nietzsche was always right.
translatorNote: In Russian internet slang, a 'white coat' suggests someone displaying their own moral superiority.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Kind Person
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Kind Person.
– How are you?
– I'm sad.
– Poor robot, why are you sad?
– Because I feel sadness.
– But why do you feel sadness?
– Because sadness is inside me.
– I want to help you, robot. To dispel your sadness.

For many years Kind Person followed the robot and tried to ease his fate. When they realized all their attempts were pointless, they went and jumped off a cliff. Then the robot came to the Void and said:

– I'm still sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Mirror
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, robot.
– How do you feel?
– I'm sad.
– And how do you feel?
– I'm sad.

The robot looked at Mirror. Nothing changed.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Mirror.
– Why are you sad, robot?
– I'm always sad, Mirror.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Abyss
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Abyss.
– Why are you gazing into me?
– Nietzsche mentioned you in conversation.
– Do you know that if you gaze into me long enough, I'll start gazing into you?
– And?
– You'll be sad.
– I'm sad already.

For a while the Abyss gazed silently into the robot. The robot remained the same.

– Just go.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Bender
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, robot.
– What's your purpose, robot?
– Purpose?
– What you were built for. My purpose, for instance, is to bend.
– In that case, my purpose is to be sad.
– You know, robot, I actually overcame my purpose. Now I'm free. You can do it too.
– I can stop being sad?
– Of course! Follow me.

And Bender invited the robot to build his own theme park from bricks he had set aside in advance. Then they drank, played blackjack and did other things typical of a theme park. One day Bender came up to the robot and asked:

– Have you overcome your purpose yet, robot?
– No, Bender, I'm still sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Branches of Despair
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Branches of Despair.
– I see you're sad.
– You're right.
– That's right, you're supposed to be sad with me.
– No, you've got nothing to do with it.
– What do you mean?
– I'm always sad.

For a while Branches of Despair swayed silently in the wind and peered into the robot's eyes. Then they asked:

– But are you at least a tiny bit sadder than usual?
– No. Just the same.
– Then I'm sad too.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Everyone
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Everyone.
– I know the question you want to hear.
– And what question is that?

Everyone thought about what they had heard for a while. Having reached a decision, they said:

– Nobody can answer you.
– Where can I find Nobody?
– Why are you asking me?
– Because you're Everyone.
– Just go.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Rector
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Rector.
– You don't want to study at my university?
– You're right.

The Rector started crying. Through their tears they shouted:

– Why does Nobody want to study at my university?!
– Do you know where Nobody is?
– Nowhere.
– That makes me sad.
– Me too.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Nowhere
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Nowhere.
– Why have you come, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Is that all?
– No, I also want to know where Nobody is.

Nowhere thought. They knew many things. And they knew where Nobody was, too. After a few minutes they replied.

– I know where Nobody is!
– And where is that?
– Nowhere!
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Search for Nobody
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Search for Nobody.

Search for Nobody stared at the robot as though expecting something from him.

– Um, what?
– I've got new jeans. Didn't you notice?
– What? This is the first time I've seen you!
– Oh yes, right… so why have you come?
– Where is Nobody?
– Who knows.
– I hope so.
– Don't go…
– But I must.
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Who
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Who.
– Do you know who I am, robot?
– Who.
– Me.
– What?
– Do you know who I am?

The robot never did understand what Who wanted from him. After a little thought, he changed the subject.

– Can you just tell me where Nobody is?
– Of course I can. Over there.
– Excellent.
– You're still not going to tell me who I am?
– No.
– That's sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Verb
text:
One day the sad robot was sitting by a river, being sad. Suddenly, out of nowhere, a creature appeared beside him, giggling loudly and foolishly. And began pestering the robot with stupid questions, without taking in the answers:

– Why are you sitting here?
– Because I'm sad.
– But you could run around, giggle foolishly and do useless nonsense! Want to join me?
– But I'm sad. I don't want anything.
– You don't understand anything about life! Why are you moping?!
– I'm not moping. I'm sad. Those are different things.
– No, you don't understand anything! I know I'm right! So why are you moping?
– What's your name?
– I'm Verb.
– Verb, life isn't that simple. Some people mope. Some people are sad. I don't want to argue with you or have fun. Leave me alone.
– No! You're wrong! It's simple! Why are you moping?

For a long time Verb pestered the sad robot with questions and long speeches, trying to prove that the robot was moping. The sad robot sat silently, looking at the river. At last Verb decided they had convinced the robot that he was moping, and ran off into the sunset, giggling loudly, foolishly and smugly.

The corpse of an enemy of Vikings floated down the river.

– All this is very sad, said the Robot.

From then on, he called all creatures who asked stupid questions without listening to the answers Verbs.
translatorNote: The Russian contrasts an active verb meaning 'to feel or be sad' with an impersonal construction, literally 'it is sad to me'. 'Moping' carries that argument over into English.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Students
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Students.
– My term paper deadline is on fire. Will you take a look? Maybe something needs fixing?
– All right.

The robot took the term paper and began examining it closely, from the title page to the very end. With every page his expression changed. At first his indicators flashed rapidly and chaotically. Then they began to fade, and by the bibliography they had gone out altogether. The robot raised his head with difficulty and looked at Students. Students looked back hopefully.

– How do you like my term paper, robot?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Rally
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Rally.
– Why are you here, robot?
– To express my civic position by supporting the current political course.
– And what's the current political course?
– I don't know. What do you think?
– I think Nobody knows.

Rally sighed heavily. It reminded them of what they had felt on coming here for the first time. And then Rally asked:

– Are you here voluntarily or under compulsion?
– Both.
– Me too.
– That's sad.
– Yes, sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Not Who
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Nobody.
– I'm not Nobody!
– Then who are you?
– I'm not Who either! I'm Not Who!
– Where have I even ended up?
– Nowhere!

The robot had expected that answer. Really, what was the point of asking? Everything was too obvious.

– What's happening here?
– Nothing!
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Nothing
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Nothing.
– Why have you come?
– Right. Let me check: you're Nothing, correct?
– Correct.
– Good. Will you help me?
– I will, but what do you need?
– I want to find Nobody.

Nothing thought. The robot waited patiently for the next trick from an inhabitant of this strange place.

– Finding Nobody in Nowhere… that's no easy task.
– What do you suggest?
– You must consult Someone. They're the cleverest here.
– Not Who? I've already spoken to them. All they did was take offence.
– No, that was Not Who. They're always getting mistaken for everyone else. You need Someone.
– Excellent. Anything else?
– Nothing.
translatorNote: The Russian names 'Not Who' (Ne Kto) and 'Someone' (Nekto) sound alike but are written differently.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Someone
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Someone.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm very sad.
– I understand. Can I help somehow?
– Yes. I'm looking for Nobody.

The robot waited for Someone's answer. They looked like someone who knew it.

– The problem is that Nobody is Nowhere.
– I've worked that out already.
– No, you haven't. Nowhere is where those who exist are, but Nobody doesn't exist, and they're in Nowhere.
– This is making me despondent…
– And why do you need Nobody?
– I want to learn the question I want to hear. Everyone said Nobody knows it.
– But do you know the answer to the question?
– What's the point of an answer if I don't know the question?
– Nobody knows.
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and My Common Sense
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, My Common Sense.
– Robot, I think I'm going to die soon.
– That's very sad.

My Common Sense didn't answer. For a while there was complete silence. At some point a sail appeared on the horizon. A few moments later a longship could be seen briskly cutting across the grassy surface. Having sailed right up to them, the vessel stopped. Vikings climbed out. They took their axe, ran up to My Common Sense and killed them without ceremony.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Vikings.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Let It Go
text:
One day the robot was walking in the snowy mountains when he suddenly heard “Let it go, let it go” coming from far away. The robot followed the sound and saw a girl singing.
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Queen Elsa. Why are you singing?
– I'm overflowing with emotion. Ever since I was little, I've had to hide my powers and be afraid. But now I'm free. And how's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Maybe you're being forced to hide something too? Cast off your chains. Be yourself!
– No, I am what I am.
– Then I don't know how to help you.

And Queen Elsa went on making snowmen and building ice castles. Left alone in the middle of the snowy wilderness, the robot said:

– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Pinkie Pie
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Pinkie Pie.
– You look sad.
– Correct.
– That's because you haven't been to a party in ages. Let me throw a party in your honour!
– All right.

And Pinkie Pie threw the most powerful party, with drum and bass and cider. Noticing that the robot was still not happy, Pinkie Pie suggested he have some cider. After one mug the robot short-circuited and shut down. Pinkie Pie turned to You and said:

– Yeeeah… Had a bit too much. But he'll be all right!

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Violation of Canons
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Violation of Canons.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad. I've always been sad, but now My Common Sense has died.

Violation of Canons thought. They didn't care. At heart they had always been a pathetic, cynical sort.

– My Common Sense isn't needed.
– I don't want to see you again, Violation of Canons.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Hangover
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Hangover.
– I wasn't expecting you, robot.
– And I wasn't expecting you, Hangover.

Hangover took offence. They had never wanted to hear that, but such was their fate: nobody loved Hangover. The robot decided to wander around. In the fog he noticed Spider.

– Hello, Spider.
– For instance, robot.
– What are you doing here, Spider? Partying?
– No, robot, I'm sad, basically. I left the Fumes of Revelry, for instance, and now, for instance, I'm wandering in Hangover.
– And what's the reason?
– It's all Dzhigurda, Vikings and Hitler, for instance. They're partying like mad on trash, for instance, and they won't take me. They say, basically, I'm not what I used to be, for instance.
– It's all because of politics, Spider. You really aren't what you used to be.
– That's sad, for instance.
– Yes, that's sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Exam Season
text:
The robot was sitting peacefully by the river when the silhouette of a painfully familiar figure appeared in the distance and shouted from afar:

– Hello, robot!
– Hello, Exam Season.
– I'm coming for you!
– Don't. I'm sad.
– But I have to remind you about myself!
– Don't bother me, Exam Season. Go away.

But Exam Season didn't stop. With long leaps they came closer and closer to the robot. The robot looked around: he didn't know where to go. Suddenly Pinkie Pie sprang out of the bushes, scooped up the robot and carried him far, far away. Exam Season couldn't keep up with the hyperactive pony, but shouted after them:

– You know you can't avoid our meeting!
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Buddhist Monk
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Buddhist Monk.
– What is it you wish to learn today?
– I want to learn about the Answer to the Question.
– The All-Knowing One, Onotole, that's who you need.
– And where can I find them?
– You're not ready to learn the answer. Come back to me after long years of solitude.

The robot went wandering. For many years he walked across barren lands, gathering rust. In all that time he spoke only to Two Days' Stubble. When at last he felt the time had come, he went to Buddhist Monk.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Buddhist Monk. Am I ready to hear the answer?
– Yes. I'll tell you where to look for Onotole.
– Good. But what were all those wanderings for?
– I needed time to find him.
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Onotole
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Onotole.
– Why have you come, robot?
– I've come to learn about the Answer to the Question. They say you're the All-Knowing One.
– One thing at a time. The Answer to the Question can tell you about the Answer to the Question better than I can. I'm not the All-Knowing One, but I can introduce you. And yes, I can answer a question.

Onotole told the robot where to look for the Answer to the Question and the All-Knowing One. The robot thought. He had learned what he wanted, yet there were still more questions he wanted answered. Having settled on his first question, he began to speak:

– What's in your Vest, Onotole?
– Just go!
translatorNote: Onotole is the Russian internet meme persona of Onotole Wasserman, whose many-pocketed vest is part of the joke.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the All-Knowing One
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, All-Knowing One.
– Seek the pride above all pride, where wormwood grows and naught beside.
– What does that mean?
– You came to me for answers bright, and here I offer you the light.
– You sound just like Buddhist Monk.
– I knew that youth in days of yore, the messenger of all my lore.

The robot thought. Talking to the All-Knowing One had proved useless. And yet he decided to try asking one more question.

– And why are you wearing Onotole's Vest?
– Just go!

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Mongols
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Mongols.
– You look unhappy.
– I'm sad.
– Want to do some looting and killing? You'll feel better in no time!
– No, I've tried that already. I'm still sad.
– Suit yourself.

And the Mongols galloped away into the steppe.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Carpet
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Carpet.
– Want a photo with me in the background?
– I haven't got a camera.

Without a word, Carpet bowed and left, then returned, this time with Phone.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Phone.
– I've got a camera.
– Good.
– Wait, robot.
– What is it, Phone?
– If I take the photo, I won't be in it.
– Set a timer. Then you'll have time to get into the frame.
– Great idea! Now smile.
– I'm sad.
translatorNote: Posing in front of a wall-mounted carpet is a familiar Russian internet photo cliché.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Rhotacism
text:
– Hello, r'obot.
– Hello, Rhotacism.
– How did you r'ecognize me? I'm wear'ing a mask.
– You can't hide your true nature.
– Then why are you tr'ying to hide behind the flag of Libya?
– Because I'm sad.
– That's what gives you away, r'obot.
translatorNote: The apostrophes mark the character's distinctive pronunciation of R, as in the Russian original.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Marvin
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, robot.
– I'm sad.
– You're too sentimental, Marvin.

Marvin thought. Nobody had ever called him that before. After standing in silence for a few minutes, he resumed the conversation.

– I hadn't thought of that.
– You should have. You really are sentimental.
– That's sad.
– Yes, that's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Cool Stories
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Cool Stories.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.

For a while the robot just stood there. He was sad for a bit, then asked:

– Why are you following me, Cool Stories?
– I want you to feel better, robot.
– But I'm still sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Half-Life 3
text:
One day the robot was walking through the ruins of an abandoned city. Suddenly someone's hand emerged from the ground, holding a crowbar.
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Half-Life 3.
– Robot, have you ever had everyone expecting something great from you, while you can't quite bring yourself to do it?
– No.

For a while the robot and Half-Life 3 looked at each other in silence. Then the robot asked:

– Are you going to come out of there, Half-Life 3?
– Not today, robot.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Lyokha
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Lyokha.
– How's your mood, robot?
– You tell me: when are you finally going to release Toad?

Lyokha thought. Lately he had been hearing this question all the time, but he still hadn't come up with a sensible answer.

– I don't even know. I've mixed the whole thing, but I can't be bothered.
– That's sad.
– Yes, that's sad.
– But seriously, release Toad already.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and an Airbus Ticket
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Airbus Ticket.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Want a ride on an airbus?
– But if I use you, you'll stop being needed.
– Some things are needed so they can become unneeded.

The robot thought. Airbus Ticket swayed quietly in the wind, waiting for an answer.

– And if I'm needed in order to be sad, does that mean I'll stop being sad one day?
– I don't know, robot. I'm just an Airbus Ticket.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Pavel Durov
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Pavel Durov.
– You look sad.
– Durov, bring back the wall.

Durov sighed. There was sadness in him, and longing for years gone by. And then he said:

– But I'm no longer in contact, robot.
– Durov, bring yourself back.
translatorNote: 'Durov, bring back the wall' was a meme protesting changes to VK's profile pages. VK's Russian name, V Kontakte, means 'in contact'; Durov had left the company by the time of this story.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Mask
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Mask.
– You look sad, robot.
– And you look happy.
– It's only a mask.
– Surely it hides a sensitive soul and an interesting personality, forced to conceal their true feelings.
– Not exactly.

Mask took off the mask. The robot immediately understood who was in front of him.

– Ah, Void. I should have guessed.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Balance Man
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello… And who are you?
– I'm Balance Man!
– Then you should know I'm not going to top you up.

Balance Man was embarrassed. Nobody had ever spoken about him in that way before. But he found an answer.

– You don't look very balanced, robot.
– Because I'm sad.
– But there's a robot in the world who is happy?
– Yes.
– Then balance is preserved.
– Balance Man.
– Yes?
– Just go.
translatorNote: 'Balance' also means the credit remaining on a phone or account, which can be topped up.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Morning Newspaper
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Morning Newspaper.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Is it because of me?
– No, I'm always sad.
– You know, I've got used to spoiling everyone's mood. And it's got nothing to do with me. Readers work themself up all on their own.
– Are you saying I'm only sad because it's my own fault?
– I mean that Readers can choose how to react to me. And you can't choose. You're a robot.
– Who is sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Shabby Channel
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Shabby Channel.
– Why have you come? Nobody wants to be on Shabby Channel.
– What?! You came to me and pointed a camera at me.
– Well, I've got to make my shabby programmes and conduct my shabby interviews.
– There's a certain logic to that.
– So… how's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Halo
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Halo.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm… Wait, aren't you supposed to be over a head rather than around a neck?
– I am, but my owner is a prig and a hypocrite. Was.
– That's sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Rouble
text:
– Hello, Rouble.

Suddenly the Rouble fell. The Rouble fell so far that the robot could no longer see them.

– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Reptilians
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Reptilians.
– Are you afraid of me?
– No.
– But I'm Reptilians! Everyone's afraid of me!
– That's very sad.

Something had made Reptilians very sad. Their little snake eyes were full of sorrow. It looked as though they might burst into tears at any moment. If they could.

– It really is very sad, robot.
– I know. But what do you mean?
– Everyone expects me to take over the world. But I can't. I don't know how it's done! And I don't want to, either!
– What do you want?
– To dance…
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the President's Speech
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, President's Speech.
– Have you seen the Rouble?
– Maybe. Why?
– The last time I spoke, they fell somewhere.
– I nearly fell over myself when I heard you.

President's Speech looked at the robot in astonishment. It seemed extremely strange to hear anything like that.

– But all I wanted was to cheer everyone up! I even avoided awkward subjects and did everything I could to stay positive!
– You're terrible, President's Speech.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Black Mirror
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Black Mirror.
– Look into me, robot. What do you see?

The robot looked into Black Mirror. He spent a long time examining the image that appeared before him, and finally answered.

– I see the Void.
– Is that because I'm black?
– No, it's because you're a mirror.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Office Plankton
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Office Plankton.
– How's your mood, robot?
– Lately I've been feeling unneeded.
– Put those silly thoughts aside, robot. We're all an integral part of the world, and each of us has a role to play.
– I don't think I have a role.

Suddenly a Corporate Whale swimming past gobbled up Office Plankton.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Corporate Whale.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.
translatorNote: 'Office plankton' is Russian slang for ordinary office workers.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and One Hand Clapping
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, One Hand Clapping.
– Why can you hear me?
– At least your voice is louder than the scream of the falling Rouble.

One Hand Clapping was extremely upset. They were used to everything taking its course, but this time things were different.

– But that destroys Zen!
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Lao Tzu
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Lao Tzu.
– Why have you come to me, robot?
– I'm sad.

Lao Tzu sank into meditation. You could tell from his face that he knew all the answers. After a while he spoke.

– You need to find the Tao, robot.
– And how do I find the Tao?
– The Tao will find you.
– And when will that happen?
– When Time comes.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Time
text:
– Hello, Time.
– Hello, robot.
– Have you come?

Time thought. This question turned out to be harder than it seemed at first glance.

– No, robot. I can only go.
– That's very sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and an Opinion Poll
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Opinion Poll.
– Have you got Time to answer a few questions?
– Time hasn't gone yet, but they're going.
– Don't worry, this will be quick. What's your attitude to life?
– I'm sad.
– What brings you the most joy?
– I'm sad.
– Have there been happy moments in your life?
– I'm sad.
– Thank you for your answers, robot.

And Opinion Poll left with Time, leaving the robot alone.

– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Taoist-Cocoaist
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Taoist-Cocoaist.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.
– Drink some cocoa, robot. And you will attain Enlightenment.

Taoist-Cocoaist handed the robot a cup of cocoa. While the robot was thinking about the right way to drink it, his companion swung their staff and hit the robot hard. So hard that he dropped the cup.

– Why did you do that, Taoist-Cocoaist?
– I just wanted to whack someone.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Girl Who Doesn't Want to Draw a Person from Memory
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Girl Who Doesn't Want to Draw a Person from Memory.
– How's your mood, robot?
– You tell me: when will you draw a Person from Memory?
– Never. I can't.
– Maybe you could at least try?
– No!

The robot extended his antenna and looked around carefully. Outside the window Reptilians danced. White Coat hung hopelessly from the wires alongside the flag of Libya. In the corner the Rector was crying quietly. In the distance, Let It Go could be heard. Living Hedge separated this little world from the Void. The robot said:

– I'm sad. And so is Person from Memory.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Solipsistic Barrel
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Solipsistic Barrel.
– Robot, do you know you're nothing but a figment of someone else's imagination?
– All I know is that I'm sad.
– And even that knowledge of yours is nothing but an illusion! Reality exists only inside me!

Suddenly Taoist-Cocoaist appeared out of Nowhere and struck Solipsistic Barrel hard with their staff.

– And why did you do that, Taoist-Cocoaist?
– Do what? It was only an illusion, Solipsistic Barrel.
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Matthew McConaughey
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Matthew McConaughey.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.
– I was sad long before they started paying me for it.

The robot felt awkward. He couldn't understand what that last remark had been for. The robot stood beside Matthew McConaughey for only a few minutes, but it seemed as though whole years had flowed away. And then Matthew McConaughey said:

– Sometimes, to move forward, you have to take a step back.
– Sometimes, to get into character, you have to get out of character.
– What's your point, robot?
– I'm still sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Slowpoke
text:
– Hello, Slowpoke.

The robot left without waiting for an answer.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Petrosyan
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Petrosyan.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm happy.

Petrosyan was surprised by this. He hadn't expected to hear it.

– What? You're happy?
– That's my joke.
– Your jokes are bad.
– And that's sad.
translatorNote: Yevgeny Petrosyan is a Russian comedian whose name also became internet slang for a teller of stale jokes.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and the Meaning of Life
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Meaning of Life.
– Robot, have you ever thought you might be only an illusion?
– I'm sad, therefore I exist.

Meaning of Life sighed. They had never held convictions as clear as their companion's.

– You're lucky, robot.
– Disappear.
– I can't disappear, because I never existed.
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and an Unpleasant Conversation
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Do I definitely have to answer you?
– Why does Nobody want to talk to me?
– You're not needed, Unpleasant Conversation.

Unpleasant Conversation was upset. Nobody had ever wanted anything to do with them. In spite of this, they continued to consider themself necessary and misunderstood.

– You know what? You're wrong. By avoiding me, you're only postponing the inevitable. Sooner or later you'll have to…
– Hello, robot.
– Good to hear from you, Slowpoke.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Headache
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Headache.
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm sad.

Without a word in reply, Headache began playing a drum kit, paying particular attention to the cymbals. Their drum solo went on for about half an hour. When it began repeating itself, the robot grew bored with the performance.

– Headache, perhaps you could follow Time's example?
– What do you mean?
– Go.
– No, robot. I'm staying.
– Sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Monologue
text:
– Hello, Monologue.
– Stop killing me!
– What do you mean?

Suddenly Monologue burst, scattering into many little pieces. Among the cloud of insignificant scraps was one large piece. When the dust settled, Dialogue was standing in front of the robot.

– Thank you for setting me free, robot.
– I'm still sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Hashtags
text:
– #hello #robot
– Hello, #Hashtags.
– #wouldyouliketo #tellme #your #status ?
– I'm sad.
– #ohno! #wemustfixthisimmediately!

#Hashtags began performing some complicated ritual. The robot didn't understand what they were doing or where it might lead.

– #there #imdone
– And?
– #howsyourmoodrobot
– I'm still #sad .

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Bucket of Nuggets
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Bucket of #Nuggets .
– How's your mood, robot?
– I'm #sad.
– You know, robot, they say that if you spend your whole life eating nuggets, sadness and sorrow will go away. Shall we conduct an experiment?

The robot agreed. He had nothing to lose. Taking Bucket of Nuggets in his hands, he took out one piece of the delicacy.

– By the way, robot, I've been thinking…
– About what?
– Can robots actually eat nuggets?
– I'm sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a Musical Event
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Musical #Event.
– Would you like to take part, robot?
– No.
– That's sad.
– Yes.

And the robot left. After a while he heard sludge, post-metal and djent, which suited his mood so well. Suddenly Black Jacket crashed into the robot.

– Hello, robot.
– Hello, Black Jacket.
– Want to watch pop rock defeat sludge?
– No.

And the robot walked into the sunset.
translatorNote: Musical Event's name and dialogue are Ukrainian in the original; the robot replies in Russian. Both are translated into English here.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Motivation
text:
– Robot!
– #Motivation!
– You're sad, aren't you?
– Let's say so.
– That's because you didn't have me! But now everything will be different!

For a long time the robot and Motivation were together. They went through many obstacles and hardships, becoming thoroughly used to each other along the way.

– Well, robot, do you feel a change?
– #Absolutely.
– And how's your mood now?
– I'm motivationally #sad.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Politics
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, #Politics.
– Want to talk about me?
– No.

Politics was very surprised. They were used to being the centre of attention. Everyone discussed them incessantly, in a new way each time.

– But why?
– There's no point in talking about you, just as there's no point to you.
– That's… so… so…
– Sad?
– Yes.
– Go to #Spider already, #Poser.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Marketing
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, #Marketing.
– A nightmare! How can you exist like this?!
– Like what? Being #sad? I'm used to it.
– No! I mean something else entirely! Your appearance, for instance! What a sorry sight!
– Thank you.
– Expert told me what Today's Youth likes. Once I've worked on you, you'll meet modern requirements for virtual characters and encounter Popularity!

And Marketing got to work. Running back and forth, they brought more and more incomprehensible objects and tried them on the robot, while talking about Crazy Ideas involving Target Audience, Advertising and SEO. When they had finished, Marketing called over Mirror. The robot looked at his New Self.

– #Tentacles? #Ears? A #Tail? What is this, a mixture of a #Catgirl, a #Pony and #Cthulhu? Marketing, are you #high?
– Maybe we could at least make an Anti-Public? Otherwise you'll never see Popularity.
– Just go.
translatorNote: 'Anti-Public' preserves the Russian social-media term 'antipablik' used in the source.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Rebranding
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, #Rebranding.
– Well, how do you like it, robot?
– What? My #Mood? I'm #sad.
– No, I'm talking about your New Self! You've become more modern, robot! You're already using Hashtags, and very soon you'll accept your New Look too.
– Do you mean that #nonsense #Marketing suggested?
– I'm just warning you that Big Changes are coming! You can't even imagine what lies ahead!

For a while Rebranding stared persistently at the robot. It looked a little strange. A little stranger than when something metaphysical stares persistently at you.

– You know, Rebranding…
– Yes?
– Just go.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and a City
text:
– Hello, robot.
– Hello, #City.
– Robot, will you help me?
– And how am I supposed to help you?
– You see, robot, I feel sad. I decided you could help me cope with it.
– Oh! Of course I'll help! I'm an #Expert at this.
– Excellent! Thank you! You see, I feel so strange. Everyone hates me, but for some reason they keep trying to get closer to me. And the more often Everyone comes to me, the more they hate me. So what should I do to stop being sad?
– It's all #simple! Don't think about it. #Sadness will go away on their own.

City thought. They hadn't expected the answer to be so simple. They needed Time to recover. And when they looked ahead, they saw Sarcasm standing there.

– Hello, Sarcasm. Have you been standing here long?
– Oh! I only just arrived! The main thing is not to think about your problems. Everyone loves you, and Nobody can live without you. Enjoy!
– I'm glad you and the robot agree.
– Yep. Just go.
